facts.statement: José Bonaparte described the species Patagopteryx deferrariisi in 1992 after receiving the fossils from Oscar de Ferrariis.
facts.quote: He passed them onto noted paleontologist José Bonaparte, who described the species Patagopteryx deferrariisi in 1992.

facts.statement: Patagopteryx lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 80 million years ago, in the Sierra Barrosa of northwestern Patagonia, Argentina.
facts.quote: Patagopteryx is an extinct monotypic genus of euornithean dinosaurs that lived during the Late Cretaceous, around 80 mya, in what is now the Sierra Barrosa in northwestern Patagonia, Argentina.

facts.statement: The skeleton of Patagopteryx shows clear indications that its ancestors were flying animals.
facts.quote: its skeleton shows clear indications that the ancestors of Patagopteryx were flying animals

facts.statement: Patagopteryx had feet with fused bones, similar to those of modern birds.
facts.quote: Patagopteryx had feet with fused bones, much like modern birds.

facts.statement: Patagopteryx lacked a furcula (wishbone), indicating it could not have possessed the muscles necessary for flight.
facts.quote: The animal did not have a furcula (wishbone), meaning it could not have had the muscles necessary for flying.

facts.statement: Patagopteryx had very short femurs, a feature characteristic of running animals.
facts.quote: The legs had very short femurs, characteristic of a running animal.

facts.statement: Patagopteryx deferrariisi lived during the Upper Cretaceous, about 85 million years ago, in the Sierra Barrosa of northwestern Patagonia, Argentina.
facts.quote: Patagopteryx deferrariisi es la única especie del género extinto Patagopteryx de ave que vivió durante el Cretácico Superior, hace cerca de 85 million years ago, en lo que ahora es Sierra Barrosa en el noroeste de la Patagonia, en Argentina.

facts.statement: Patagopteryx is significant because it documents a distinct lineage of basal birds and, known through multiple specimens, constitutes the best-represented Mesozoic bird in the Southern Hemisphere.
facts.quote: Patagopteryx es importante no solo porque documenta un linaje diferenciado de aves basales, sino también porque, al conocerse a través de varios ejemplares, constituye el ave mesozoica mejor representada del hemisferio sur.

facts.statement: Today, although still considered a bird, Patagopteryx is isolated in a separate family or order within the Ornithuromorpha.
facts.quote: Hoy en día, si bien se sigue considerando como un ave, está aislada en una familia u orden separados dentro de los Ornithuromorpha.

facts.statement: The time range for Patagopteryx is the Santonian stage, from 85.7 to 83.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Santonian to Santonian (85.7 to 83.6 million years ago)

facts.statement: It is debated whether Patagopteryx represents the earliest example of secondary flightlessness, as other studies suggest earlier diverging theropods may also have been secondarily flightless.
facts.quote: though other studies find earlier diverging theropods to be secondarily flightless.
